The '''Copa Colombia''' ({{langx|en|Colombia Cup|link=yes}}), officially known as '''Copa BetPlay Dimayor''', is an annual [[association football|football]] tournament in [[Colombia]]. It is contested by the 36 professional clubs affiliated to the [[División Mayor del Fútbol Profesional Colombiano]] (DIMAYOR) and is the nation's domestic cup competition, equivalent to the [[FA Cup]] in England or the [[Copa del Rey]] in Spain.

The Copa Colombia was played for the first time in 1950, and it has been played consecutively since its revival in 2008. Throughout history, the '''Copa Colombia''' name has been used to refer to several tournaments or trophies:

* A [[double-elimination tournament|double-elimination]], knockout tournament parallel to the [[Categoría Primera A|Colombian league]], which was played from 1950–51 to 1952–53.
* A tournament that was played under a round-robin group format in which teams advanced to a final group, which was also named as ''Copa Presidente de la República'', played from late 1956 to early 1957.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=g58cAAAAIBAJ&sjid=y2gEAAAAIBAJ&hl=es&pg=914%2C1376192 |title=Cayó el campeón profesional en Cali |trans-title=The professional champion fell in Cali |newspaper=Intermedio |publisher=El Tiempo |page=14 |date=12 November 1956 |access-date=16 August 2023 |location=Bogotá |archive-date=23 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221123234526/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=g58cAAAAIBAJ&sjid=y2gEAAAAIBAJ&hl=es&pg=914,1376192 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* A commemorative trophy awarded to [[Millonarios F.C.|Millonarios]] in 1963, which is not considered a Copa Colombia title.<ref name="#1">{{cite web |last1=Ascencio |first1=José Orlando |title=Las copas que no son... (Opinión) |trans-title=The cups that are not... (Opinion) |url=http://www.eltiempo.com/deportes/columnistas-deportes/jose-orlando-ascencio/las-copas-que-no-son-opinion-columna-jose-orlando-ascencio-53275 |publisher=[[El Tiempo (Colombia)|El Tiempo]] |language=es |date=30 January 2017 |access-date=16 August 2023 |archive-date=17 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230817045725/https://www.eltiempo.com/deportes/columnistas-deportes/jose-orlando-ascencio/las-copas-que-no-son-opinion-columna-jose-orlando-ascencio-53275 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* A tournament played in 1981 and 1989, which was part of the league season and awarded bonus points or berths to the final stages of the league tournament.<ref name="#1"/>
* The knockout tournament played by teams in [[Categoría Primera A]] and [[Categoría Primera B]], established since [[2008 Copa Colombia|2008]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Estos han sido los campeones de la Copa Colombia |trans-title=These have been the Copa Colombia champions |url=https://www.eltiempo.com/archivo/documento/CMS-16435417 |publisher=El Tiempo |language=es |date=19 November 2015 |access-date=16 August 2023 |archive-date=9 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409225702/https://www.eltiempo.com/archivo/documento/CMS-16435417 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Atlético Nacional]] are the current holders, who won their [[2025 Copa Colombia|eighth Copa Colombia]] title against [[Independiente Medellín]], winning the final series by a 1–0 aggregate score. Atlético Nacional are also the most successful club in the competition.

== History ==
=== Copa Colombia in "El Dorado" ===
The Copa Colombia was an idea promoted in 1950 by [[División Mayor del Fútbol Profesional Colombiano|DIMAYOR]] at the time known as "[[El Dorado (Colombian football)|El Dorado]]" due to the boom experienced by football in the country. It emerged as an official tournament to be held annually, independent from the league championship and under a particular knockout format in which teams were divided by proximity into territorial groups of four teams each. Teams faced each other in home-and-away matches to determine the teams that advanced to a stage known as the winners' round. When a team lost two ties it was eliminated, while if it won it played a new round. The worst of the three remaining teams was eliminated, while a new tie was played, called losers' round, to determine the other team that reached the final. Due to the economic power of clubs and the Colombian league at that time, many teams had large payrolls for both tournaments as well as the international games they played. However, the little interest the competition generated among the participants led to delays in the scheduling of games and the first tournament ended in 1951.<ref name="CP">{{cite web |last1=Arenas Vásquez |first1=Paolo |title=La Copa Postobón no es la Copa Colombia |trans-title=The Copa Postobón is not the Copa Colombia |url=http://www.copapostobon.com.co/noticia/la-copa-postobon-no-es-la-copa-colombia-03697 |publisher=Copa Postobón |access-date=16 August 2023 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130101171712/http://www.copapostobon.com.co/noticia/la-copa-postobon-no-es-la-copa-colombia-03697#selection-227.0-227.39 |archive-date=1 January 2013 |language=es |date=9 November 2012}}</ref> It was the reason why the next edition was not held until 1952, and its conclusion was again delayed until the following year.

In the period between both editions (1951–52), what turned out to be the early rounds of the 1952–53 edition is mistakenly referred as another edition of the competition due to its [[double-elimination tournament|double-elimination]] format.<ref name="El Cinco Cero">{{cite web |title=Historia y campeones de la Copa Colombia |trans-title=History and champions of the Copa Colombia |url=https://elcincocero.com/historia-y-campeones-de-la-copa-colombia/ |publisher=El Cinco Cero |access-date=16 August 2023 |language=es |archive-date=17 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230817045724/https://elcincocero.com/historia-y-campeones-de-la-copa-colombia/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Boca Juniors de Cali]] (as winners of the winners' round) and [[Millonarios F.C.|Millonarios]] (who were defeated by Boca Juniors in the winners' round but then went on to win the losers' round) played the final of the 1952–53 edition, which was ultimately won by Millonarios. Following that edition, the tournament was cancelled due to the lack of interest displayed by fans and teams alike.<ref name="Comutricolor">{{cite web |title=La Copa Postobón no es la Copa Colombia |trans-title=The Copa Postobón is not the Copa Colombia |url=https://comutricolor.com/copa-postobon-no-es-copa-colombia/ |publisher=Comutricolor |access-date=16 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110061712/https://comutricolor.com/copa-postobon-no-es-copa-colombia/ |archive-date=10 November 2017 |language=es |date=17 November 2013}}</ref>

An attempt to resume it was made in 1956–57: in said third edition, the first phase was played and six teams qualified to play a final hexagonal: [[Atlético Nacional]], [[Independiente Santa Fe|Santa Fe]], [[Deportivo Pereira]], Boca Juniors de Cali and the ones that would be the top two of said hexagonal: [[Independiente Medellín]] and [[Atlético Bucaramanga]]; however, the grand final between these two teams was never played, thus the tournament was abandoned and no more editions were played until the 1980s.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=NSQhAAAAIBAJ&sjid=VGgEAAAAIBAJ&hl=es&pg=4808%2C269853 |title=Calendario Final de la Copa Colombia |trans-title=The Copa Colombia's Final Fixture |newspaper=Intermedio |publisher=El Tiempo |page=14 |date=4 January 1957 |access-date=16 August 2023 |location=Bogotá |archive-date=24 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221124162130/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=NSQhAAAAIBAJ&sjid=VGgEAAAAIBAJ&hl=es&pg=4808,269853 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Commemorative cup (1963) ===
After consecutively winning the league titles in [[1961 Campeonato Profesional|1961]], [[1962 Campeonato Profesional|1962]] and [[1963 Campeonato Profesional|1963]], [[Millonarios F.C.|Millonarios]] were granted permanent ownership of the "Copa Colombia" trophy, which should have been awarded to the winner of three editions. As these editions did not come to fruition, Millonarios were awarded the trophy on account of their league success.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=vd4cAAAAIBAJ&sjid=pWMEAAAAIBAJ&hl=es&pg=5554%2C3954542 |title=La Copa Colombia, Propiedad Definitiva de los Celestes |trans-title=The Copa Colombia, Definitive Property of the Sky Blues |newspaper=El Tiempo |page=18 |date=20 December 1963 |access-date=16 August 2023 |location=Bogotá |archive-date=18 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170318141606/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=vd4cAAAAIBAJ&sjid=pWMEAAAAIBAJ&hl=es&pg=5554,3954542 |url-status=live }}</ref> Although the club counts it as a title, it is not recognized as an official title by DIMAYOR.<ref name="El Cinco Cero"/>

In 2017, and through its Twitter account, DIMAYOR included said trophy among those won by manager [[Gabriel Ochoa Uribe]] (who coached the club in 1963), without clarifying whether it is an official title.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=DIMAYOR|user=Dimayor|number=932654054840455168|title=Felicitamos al médico, Gabriel Ochoa Uribe que hoy cumple 88 años. Es el entrenador con más títulos del Fútbol Colombiano. 13 campeonatos: @AmericadeCali (7), @MillosFCoficial (5) y @SantaFe (1). Además, consiguió una Copa Colombia con los azules.|trans-title=We congratulate the physician, Gabriel Ochoa Uribe who turns 88 today. He is the manager with the most titles in Colombian Football. 13 championships: @AmericadeCali (7), @MillosFCoficial (5) and @SantaFe (1). Besides, he got a Copa Colombia with the ''blues''.|language=es|date=20 November 2017|access-date=16 August 2023}}</ref>

=== 1980s: Copa Colombia as part of the league tournament ===
In 1981, an event with the same name was held again but with the particularity that it was played by the 10 clubs eliminated from the final quadrangular of the [[Categoría Primera A|Campeonato Profesional]] (made up of 14 teams), as an appendix phase of the championship. Firstly, the six teams eliminated in the regular phase participated in a hexagonal from which one team ([[Independiente Medellín]]) qualified for the final, with the other finalist ([[Deportivo Cali]]) being decided in a quadrangular between the four teams that were eliminated in the semifinal phase. Independiente Medellín won the tournament after beating Deportivo Cali 3–1 in the first leg and a 1–1 draw in the second leg, both played in [[Medellín]]. The competition had an incentive for the first time, awarding a spot in the league's final octagonal for the following season, which Independiente Medellín did not need in the end since they ultimately qualified through league performance.<ref name="CP"/> In 2014, this tournament was officially recognized by the [[Colombian Football Federation]] as part of the tribute that [[CONMEBOL]] paid to Independiente Medellín for its 101st anniversary.<ref>{{cite web |title=CONMEBOL rinde homenaje al DIM en sorteo de la Libertadores |trans-title=CONMEBOL pays tribute to DIM at the Libertadores draw |url=http://www.fcf.com.co/index.php/la-federacion/1783-conmebol-rinde-homenaje-al-dim-en-sorteo-de-la-libertadores |publisher=[[Colombian Football Federation]] |access-date=16 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180214073748/http://www.fcf.com.co/index.php/la-federacion/1783-conmebol-rinde-homenaje-al-dim-en-sorteo-de-la-libertadores |archive-date=14 February 2018 |language=es |date=14 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Independiente de Medellín cumple 101 años de vida institucional |trans-title=Independiente from Medellín celebrates 101 years of institutional life |url=https://www.conmebol.com/noticias/independiente-de-medellin-cumple-101-ano-de-vida-institucional/ |publisher=[[CONMEBOL]] |language=es |date=14 November 2014 |access-date=16 August 2023}}</ref>

In 1989, a new Copa Colombia edition was held, again as part of the [[1989 Campeonato Profesional|league championship]]. It was played between the first and second rounds of the tournament and the points from this competition were added to the league's aggregate table, through which eight teams would qualify for the final stage of the championship. However, that year's tournament was abandoned due to the assassination of referee Álvaro Ortega. The Copa's first stage was played in three regional groups of five teams each, and the top eight in the tournament's table qualified for a knockout stage. [[Independiente Santa Fe|Santa Fe]] won the competition by beating [[Unión Magdalena]] in the final, and was awarded 0.5 bonus points.<ref>{{cite web |title=Re-post: Santa Fé campeón de la última Copa Colombia |trans-title=Re-post: Santa Fe champion of the last Copa Colombia |url=https://bestiariodelbalon.com/2009/11/14/558/ |publisher=[[Bestiario del balón]] |language=es |date=14 November 2009 |access-date=16 August 2023}}</ref> The runners-up, Unión Magdalena, were awarded 0.375 bonus points, whilst semi-finalists [[Atlético Junior|Junior]] and [[América de Cali]] were awarded 0.250 and 0.125 bonus points, respectively.<ref name="CP"/>

=== Reinstatement in 2008 ===
On 14 February 2008, the 36 member clubs of DIMAYOR approved the holding of a new tournament known as Copa Colombia, integrating the teams competing in the [[Categoría Primera A|Primera A]] and [[Categoría Primera B|Primera B]] tiers of Colombian professional football. In its first editions, it granted the winner a berth into the following season's [[Copa Sudamericana]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dimayor aprobó la realización de la Copa Colombia que arrancará el 12 de marzo |trans-title=Dimayor approved the holding of the Copa Colombia that will start on 12 March |url=https://caracol.com.co/radio/2008/02/14/deportes/1203004260_548799.html |publisher=[[Caracol Radio]] |language=es |date=14 February 2008 |access-date=16 August 2023 |archive-date=17 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230817045713/https://caracol.com.co/radio/2008/02/14/deportes/1203004260_548799.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Starting from its [[2017 Copa Colombia|2017 edition]], it granted its winner a place in the [[Copa Libertadores]] for the following season. The only exception to this was the [[2020 Copa Colombia|2020 edition]], which awarded its winner a berth into the [[2022 Copa Sudamericana]] given that the tournament was temporarily suspended due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia|COVID-19 pandemic]] and did not end within the calendar year. Qualification for the Copa Libertadores was granted to the winners until the [[2023 Copa Colombia|2023 edition]], with the 36 DIMAYOR member clubs deciding that the winners of the [[2024 Copa Colombia]] would qualify for the Copa Sudamericana.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.futbolred.com/futbol-colombiano/copa-betplay/polemica-por-decisiones-dimayor-sobre-copa-colombia-betplay-2024-campeon-no-jugara-libertadores-196468|title=¿Dimayor 'mató' la Copa BetPlay? Polémica por decisión en asamblea|trans-title=Did Dimayor 'kill' the Copa BetPlay? Controversy for assembly decision|publisher=Futbolred|language=es|date=13 December 2023|access-date=13 February 2024|archive-date=13 February 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240213215729/https://www.futbolred.com/futbol-colombiano/copa-betplay/polemica-por-decisiones-dimayor-sobre-copa-colombia-betplay-2024-campeon-no-jugara-libertadores-196468|url-status=live}}</ref>
